Size fuses slow-blow (Class-T) so that same surge does not nuisance-trip them.Charge controller & protectionController capacity50 A total — one 60 A MPPT controllerController noteMany low-frequency hybrid inverters have an MPPT charger built in — check its max PV input covers these amps before buying a separate controller.Main battery fuse/breaker60 A (bank can pull ~21 A at full load)PV disconnect60 ABattery-to-inverter cable (copper)2 m run10 (5.26 mm²) or larger5 m run10 (5.26 mm²) or larger10 m run6 (13.3 mm²) or largerArray Mounting & Optimal TiltArray orientationFace True South (180°) for maximum annual solar harvestYear-round fixed tilt~19° from horizontalWinter steep tilt (critical for off-grid)~36° — sheds snow & captures low winter sunSummer tilt (optional)~10°Mounting recommendationRoof mount (flush/racked) or ground mount🛡️ Essential Balance-of-System (BOS) & Safety ChecklistDC Battery DisconnectHeavy-duty rotary disconnect switch + Class-T fuse (or DC-rated breaker) sized to 60 A near battery positive terminal.PV Array Isolator + SPDDC-rated 2-pole breaker and DC Surge Protective Device (lightning arrestor) before the charge controller.Battery Shunt / MonitorPrecision 500 A shunt on main battery negative for exact State-of-Charge (SoC) tracking (voltage alone is inaccurate on lithium).Copper Busbars & CablesSolid copper busbars for multi-battery paralleling; hydraulic hex crimps with dual-wall adhesive heatshrink on all battery cable lugs.Equipment GroundingCommon earth ground bonding for panel mounting rails, lightning arrestors, and inverter chassis to ground rod.Inverter sized from AVERAGE load (no appliance peak entered) — real spikes (kettle, fridge start, pump surge) can be several times higher. Enter appliances for an exact peak. 48 V class: what any house-scale system uses — lowest current for the same power. Educational estimate from your sizing result — not an engineering design, not a shopping order. Fuse and cable figures assume copper, conservative ampacity, and a short battery-to-inverter run; verify everything against your local electrical code with a licensed professional before buying or energizing anything. How this was calculated Data: NASA POWER MERRA2/SYN1DEG via power.larc.nasa.gov, hourly 2021–2025. Derates applied: soiling 97%, wiring 98%, mismatch 99%, MPPT 98%. Cell temperature model: NOCT 45°C, power temperature coefficient -0.34%/°C. Inverter efficiency 94%. Charging blocked below chemistry's cold limit (LFP 0°C). Load basis: direct kWh entry. Costs span ex-factory China through PowMr-class budget retail (cell market indications → PowMr public catalog, Aug 2026) - the low end is components before freight/duty/BMS, the high end is shipped retail with BMS and enclosure included. Auto mode sizes sodium-ion and LFP to deliver the same bill cut within its depth-of-discharge window (sodium modeled on LFP voltage settings — slightly less capacity, gentler discharge). The 60/80/95% matrix columns are fixed reference points; the "your target" column follows the 1–150% slider and is sized by an exact engine run. Lifetime cost adds every bank swap PLUS install labor each time over 20 years; lead-acid is modeled WITHOUT active balancing (typical DIY strings) and shown only as a savings reference, never recommended. Payback compares first cost against bill savings; fixed connection fees not counted. Capacity model at this site's mean 25°C: LFP 100%, sodium-ion 85% (LFP voltage settings), lead-acid (AGM) about 85% (cold derating where applicable). Rate source: open.er-api.com, as of Nov 14, 2026 — that date is the exchange rate’s; the weather figures are five years of hourly history. Amounts shown in USD at 1 per US$1. Energy cost rates and recommendations are converted to USD; source price scopes remain USD-denominated. Grid spend assumes $0.44/kWh at 10 kWh/day. No incentives or subsidies are included — these are unsubsidised costs. Electricity prices are assumed flat for 20 years — no rate rises are projected. Surplus is credited at the hourly tariff — not at a time-of-use schedule or annual netting.
